title: Lesson Two: Why Teach Financial Literacy?
coreMove: Judge money decisions by cash direction: assets feed you, liabilities bill you, and income alone cannot fix a leaking pattern.

exampleSpecs.stakes: see cash movement before another purchase gets a flattering name
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist uses the income statement and balance sheet to classify cash direction

exampleSpecs.audience: buyers treating a residence as automatic wealth
exampleSpecs.stakes: love the home without misreading its cash-flow role
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates the house's life value from its monthly outflows

exampleSpecs.audience: high earners tempted to scale spending
exampleSpecs.stakes: convert a raise into freedom rather than a larger trap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees taxes, cars, and credit rising with salary

exampleSpecs.audience: owners deciding whether growth strengthens the statement
exampleSpecs.stakes: avoid confusing busy ownership with asset creation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist checks whether the new project adds cash to the asset side

exampleSpecs.stakes: separate pride in a house from the cash it requires
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist corrects an investment label by listing mortgage, property taxes, and repairs

exampleSpecs.audience: workers whose income rises faster than their assets
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep a promotion from becoming a larger monthly obligation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist changes the sequence after seeing salary, taxes, cars, and credit move together
